newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia's Sihanouk says abdication offer rejected.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk says abdication offer rejected.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk said on Wednesday that his offer to abdicate had been refused by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen although his decision to return soon to his homeland had been welcomed.

"This delegation -- in particular his excellency Hun Sen -- assured N. Sihanouk of its fidelity and its support for the king, whose offer to abdicate it did not accept," Sihanouk said in a statement sent to reporters in Beijing.

Political analysts said Sihanouk's offer on Monday to abdicate could signal he did not want any part of current events in Cambodia. Hun Sen last month overthrew his original co-prime minister, the king's son Prince Norodom Ranariddh, plunging the Southeast Asian nation into turmoil.

Sihanouk's statement followed a meeting on Tuesday with a high-level Cambodian delegation led by Hun Sen at the monarch's residence in Beijing, where he has been receiving medical treatment since February.
Political analysts in Phnom Penh said Hun Sen had been seeking approval for his new government from Sihanouk, but it was not clear whether he had received this.
In an earlier statement, Sihanouk said he had asked Hun Sen to end the violence in Cambodia and work toward national reconciliation.
"I asked all of them to try to make an effort to achieve peace, cool down the situation and end war, insecurity and violence," Sihanouk said.

The king said he had asked Hun Sen and newly appointed First Prime Minister Ung Huot "to somehow achieve non-violence, national reconciliation, peaceful co-existence, solidarity, mutual respect, respect for human rights and our national constitution".

Last week Sihanouk, expressing strong disapproval of recent events in his country, called Ung Huot a "puppet" of Hun Sen and said he was dismayed by what had happened in Cambodia. He likened the situation to a "comedy".
A Cambodian military court has since issued a warrant for Prince Ranariddh's arrest on charges of weapons smuggling.

A brief statement from the Cambodian delegation issued by the Ministry of Information in Phnom Penh said Sihanouk had asked the delegation to assure Cambodians that the king was "working with all the people in the country".

Sihanouk said the delegation welcomed his plan to return home soon to visit the northern Cambodian town of Siem Reap, home to the famed temple complex of Angkor, to hold a Buddhist ceremony for peace and reconciliation.
"(This delegation) expressed its infinite gratitude for the royal decision to return to Cambodia in the near future," Sihanouk said.
He said he had no plans for another meeting with Hun Sen after holding five hours of talks on Tuesday.
The Cambodian delegation also met China's First Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Tang Jiaxuan, who was quoted in a statement as saying that recent events in Cambodia were an internal affair.
Hun Sen's delegation arrived in Beijing on Monday and was scheduled to return to Phnom Penh on Thursday.
